title: Singapore’s Lee Kuan Yew’s fountain pen valued at US$23,000-US$39,000 up for auction
snippet: A silver Montblanc fountain pen owned by Singapore’s founding prime minister Lee Kuan Yew is up for auction with a starting bid of S$20,000. Singapore auction house Hotlotz said on Wednesday that the pen, engraved “SM Lee Kuan Yew”, was previously sold at the Lee Kuan Yew Family Collection charity auction in July 2003. Hotlotz has valued the silver Montblanc Meisterstuck No 146 fountain pen at S$30,000 (US$23,000) to S$50,000 (US$39,000). At the 2003 charity auction, it was estimated at S$4,000.

title: China Hits Back at US With Tighter Drone Export Curbs, Sanctions
snippet: China tightened its exports controls on drones to the US and sanctioned multiple American companies in a series of retaliatory measures against Washington’s widening tech curbs.

title: Trump Fuels Hopes of Hormuz Reopening With Hints a Deal is Near
snippet: US President Donald Trump said a deal on the Strait of Hormuz is possible as early as Wednesday, as expectations build for an arrangement that allows for the reopening of the crucial waterway for energy markets.

title: How the French government is convincing banks to loan Le Pen funds for her campaign
snippet: A consortium of banks should allow far-right candidate Marine Le Pen to obtain a loan in France. In past campaigns, she took loans from Russian and Hungarian establishments after French banks were reluctant to be associated with her.
